gallery/dataclass_adapter.critique: Names the class and lists every field=value pair exactly as extracted in meta; nothing missing, nothing invented.

gallery/decimal_number.critique: Value and 9-digit precision both correct and match meta exactly; nothing else in meta (sign, exponent) is essential to add.

gallery/defaultdict_metadata.critique: Surfaces default_factory, key/value types, and the actual key names since all 3 keys fit within the sample; a complete picture.

gallery/deque_metadata.critique: Front/back samples now shown, giving a real sense of contents; count alone would have been vacuous.

gallery/enum_adapter.critique: Names enum class, active member, and sibling members with count; concise and fully matches meta.

gallery/float_probability_pattern.critique: Surfaces the probability pattern classification, the single most interesting fact about this value.

gallery/fraction_number.critique: Correct and crisp; omits the float approximation (~3.14159) from meta which would help decimal-minded readers, but the fraction itself is the primary fact and is stated clearly.

gallery/function_adapter.critique: Now shows full signature with type hints and the docstring, the two most useful facts about a callable; slightly verbose with both 'callable function' and the docstring quoted in full but still clear.

gallery/int_special_year.critique: Surfaces the year classification instead of a bare int value.

gallery/io_bytesio_adapter.critique: Type and size are correct and the core facts; stream position (0) is free to add and a content hint would help since size alone is thin for a buffer.

gallery/io_stringio_adapter.critique: Correct type and length in one clean sentence; cursor position (0) from meta is omitted and a short content preview would add value but isn't available in meta.

Accurate but describes the wrapper, not the content: for HTML('

Hi

') a user wants 'an IPython HTML display object' plus a content hint/length. Listing the raw method name '_repr_html_' is implementation-speak; the object_type (IPython.core.display.HTML) already says it more plainly.

gallery/jax_adapter.critique: Adds dtype alongside shape, the standard pairing for array summaries.

gallery/json_string.critique: States valid JSON, top-level object type, and names all keys — exactly what's needed for a short JSON string, nothing extraneous.

gallery/list_of_dicts_schema.critique: Correctly identifies record count and consistent-schema pattern, but meta has the exact schema (city:str, id:int, population:int) and doesn't name a single field or type.

gallery/list_of_ints_summary.critique: Now includes accurate range/mean/std stats computed over the full 29-item list (fixed a prior sampling bug that would have understated the range).

gallery/long_string_markdown_document.critique: Adds line and word counts alongside char count and correctly identifies the markdown document type; concise one-liner.

gallery/matplotlib_adapter.critique: Now names the chart type (line plot) alongside subplot count and fixes the pluralization slip; uses the plot_types/num_lines metadata that was previously discarded.

gallery/matplotlib_axes_inference.critique: Correctly names both scatter and bar/histogram plot types, no longer identical to the image+hist case; same bar/histogram ambiguity caveat as the sibling case.

gallery/networkx_adapter_nl.critique: Node and edge counts are the right headline. Metadata also has is_directed=false and density=1.0; saying 'undirected' would complete it. Minor grammar: '1 edges'.

gallery/numpy_1d_array.critique: Shape, dtype, head/tail sample, and now stats (range/mean/std) are all present; a complete picture of the array in one line.

gallery/numpy_2d_array.critique: Corner sample plus stats now appended, exactly the improvement the prior critique asked for.

gallery/numpy_scalar.critique: Ideal for a scalar: type, dtype, and value in one short sentence. Nothing missing, nothing extra.

gallery/ordered_dict_metadata.critique: Fixes the prior grammar bug ('A ordered_dict') and now surfaces the str->int mapping and value stats (range 0-25, mean 9.2); correctly omits the key list since 6 keys exceeds the 5-item sample.

gallery/pandas_categorical.critique: Surfaces ordered=True (via 'ordered categories'), category labels, and the skewed per-category counts, the real story of this Categorical.

gallery/pandas_dataframe_metadata.critique: Excellent: shape, per-column dtype/nulls/stats/cardinality, and a sample row. Minor noise: 'Memory: 183.0 B' is filler for a 3-row frame, and quoting like {'a': '1.0', 'b': "'x'"} double-wraps values.

gallery/pandas_index_types.critique: Surfaces name, dtype, and sample values instead of a bare entry count; a data-savvy user gets what they need in one line.

gallery/pandas_series_metadata.critique: Model summary: name, length, nulls, dtype, stats, and sample all in one tight line. Couldn't ask for more from a 4-value Series.

gallery/pathlib_adapter.critique: Correctly identifies a 1-line, 5 B text file with no invented details, but omits the cheap, available filename and content preview ('hello') that meta already has.

gallery/pil_image_adapter.critique: Exactly what you want for an image: dimensions and mode. Format is None in meta so there is nothing more to say.

gallery/pil_image_list_adapter.critique: Now shows the per-image sizes and mode, surfacing the varying-size story (uniform_size false) that mattered most.

gallery/polars_adapter_nl.critique: Shape, full schema with Polars dtypes, and a sample row -- everything a user needs for a 2x2 frame, nothing wasted.

gallery/purepath_adapter.critique: Correctly flags it as a pure (non-filesystem) path and shows the path itself. Could add the .txt suffix or note it never touches the filesystem, but for a PurePath there is little more to say.

gallery/pyarrow_table.critique: Rows, columns, schema with Arrow types, and a sample row -- the complete picture in one line. Memory is borderline filler at 26 B but harmless.

gallery/pydantic_adapter_nl.critique: Lists field names with actual values (name, role, salary, years, skills) instead of only the class name, matching the earlier attrs fix.

gallery/pytorch_adapter_nl.critique: Adds dtype and device to the shape, giving the standard tensor-summary trio.

gallery/range_metadata.critique: Start/stop/step fully specify the range and are stated plainly; omitting the length (20, in meta) leaves a small bit of mental arithmetic to the reader.

gallery/regex_match_adapter.critique: Accurate match text and span; could mention the two capture groups (48213, 2026-07-30) present in meta but the one-liner still covers the essentials.

gallery/regex_pattern_adapter.critique: Pattern text and group count (3) both match meta exactly with no escaping bugs this time; could optionally name the capture groups (year, month, day) which are in groupindex.

gallery/requests_adapter_nl.critique: Status 200 is correct, but the URL (https://example.com) is in the meta and is the first thing a user wants; the summary omits it entirely. Add the URL (and content-type when present).

gallery/scipy_sparse_csr.critique: nnz and density were already present and correct; format/shape/nnz/density together fully describe a sparse matrix concisely.

gallery/short_string_url_pattern.critique: Correctly flags the URL pattern and shows the full value, ideal for a short string; minor imprecision saying the string 'contains' a URL when it IS one.

gallery/tensorflow_adapter.critique: Adds dtype (now cleanly formatted as 'float32' instead of the old repr) and the small sample values array for a 6-element tensor.

gallery/time_adapter.critique: Correct value and the naive/aware distinction is exactly what matters for a time object. 'Timezone: naive.' as a separate clipped sentence reads slightly telegraphic; fold it in ('a naive time: 14:30:00').

gallery/timedelta_adapter.critique: Fixed the internal-inconsistency bug: now correctly reports the 5.5-hour remainder (5 hours 30 minutes) matching total_seconds=1488600.

gallery/traceback_adapter.critique: Excellent content: frame count, file:line, function, and the raising line. Two nits: '1 frames' is a pluralization bug, and the summary shows where the raise happened but not the exception type/message (ValueError('boom')).

gallery/tuple_metadata.critique: Shows element types and actual sample values for a small 5-tuple instead of a bare count; exactly what the prior critique asked for.

gallery/uuid_adapter.critique: Version and full value are exactly what a user wants from a UUID; nothing missing, nothing extraneous.

gallery/xml_string.critique: Correctly identifies valid XML and names the root tag, the right headline fact for a short document; length omitted but not critical.

gallery/yaml_string.critique: Correctly validates YAML and lists all four keys accurately; noting it parses to a dict (in meta) would be a small additional signal.

real/local_archive.critique: Accurate and crisp, but with only 1 entry the metadata already names it (NLSY.dta); naming that single entry in the sentence would be far more informative for essentially no added length, still unchanged from before this behavior change.

real/local_nlsy.critique: Correctly identifies the Stata format, observation/variable counts, and lists all 14 variable names from a header-only sniff without loading the file; unchanged in substance from before this behavior change.

real/penguins_deep.critique: Shape, total null count, and now the sex column (11 nulls, the largest NA source) surfaced first with bill_length_mm/bill_depth_mm, directly addressing the earlier gap where the null-heaviest column was omitted from the prose; species/island categorical detail no longer fits in the 3-column cap but remains visible in the sample row.

real/titanic_deep.critique: Row/col/null totals and top-3 column profiles (survived, pclass, sex) are accurate, but the column detail cuts off before showing the dataset's defining nulls (age: 177, deck: ~688) that drive the 869 total; should prioritize columns with nulls or high info over the first three.

real/titanic_shallow.critique: All 15 columns and inferred types are correctly listed from the header/sample line alone, with a clear tip on how to get the deep profile; concise single-sentence shallow summary for a real messy CSV.
